paper_role: prospective Paper 2 extension after E6; no manuscript claim change unless promotion gate passes
question: Can multiple independent local plant-pollinator systems be harmonized onto a common temperature-response effect-size contract, so the local-information side of E6 is no longer represented by one large study?
design_principle: Do not pool bird and plant-pollinator rows merely because both are expressed in days per degree C.
Build a multi-study local interaction meta-analysis first; compare it with the Usui migration-distance result only after source-level effects and dependence are reconstructed.
Never convert snowmelt, degree-day, annual-trend and temperature effects into one metric without an explicit defensible transformation.

A.unit: days of relative timing / degree C
A.definition: direct temperature sensitivity of plant-pollinator relative timing or synchrony

B.definition: pollinator temperature slope minus plant temperature slope estimated against a matched temperature exposure in the same system

C.definition: long-term synchrony trend when no commensurate temperature estimand is recoverable

candidate_sources.citation: Freimuth et al. 2022, Climate warming changes synchrony of plants and pollinators
candidate_sources.system: Germany; plants plus beetles, flies, bees, butterflies/moths
candidate_sources.current_state: E6 source already reconstructed; group means and 1763 species slopes frozen
candidate_sources.caveat: interaction-level synchrony is derived from predicted pairings; retain pair/study dependence

candidate_sources.citation: Bartomeus et al. 2013, Biodiversity ensures plant-pollinator phenological synchrony against climate change
candidate_sources.system: apple flowering and native bee pollinators; 46-year historical series
candidate_sources.current_state: public Dryad bytes identified; schema not yet reconstructed
candidate_sources.caveat: verify whether temperature exposure needed for Tier A is included or must be reconstructed

candidate_sources.citation: Xie et al. 2025, Shifting spring ephemeral pollination windows under climate change - a three-body problem
candidate_sources.system: Claytonia virginica flowering and specialist bee Andrena erigeniae occurrence across eastern North American ecoregions
candidate_sources.current_state: public Zenodo raw data plus source R code identified; published matched temperature sensitivities in d/C

winter_minimum_temperature_C.note: 2025 paper reports approximate average advances; source R code fits matched winter minimum and spring average temperature models with ecoregion random slopes

candidate_sources.caveat: temperature effects vary by ecoregion and interact with precipitation; primary E7 extraction must use a declared common climatic reference point or ecoregion-level matched slopes, not a single unqualified global difference

candidate_sources.citation: Kehrberger & Holzschuh 2019, Warmer temperatures advance flowering in a spring plant more strongly than emergence of two solitary spring bee species
candidate_sources.system: 11 grasslands; one spring plant and two Osmia bee species
candidate_sources.current_state: public Dryad workbook identified; schema not yet reconstructed
candidate_sources.caveat: site-temperature gradient rather than long time series; keep study design as moderator

candidate_sources.citation: Kudo & Cooper 2019, When spring ephemerals fail to meet pollinators
candidate_sources.system: Corydalis ambigua and overwintered bumble bees; 19 years plus snow-removal experiment
candidate_sources.current_state: public Dryad workbook identified; mechanistic anchor
candidate_sources.caveat: primary driver includes snowmelt and accumulated degree-days; do not force into days per degree C unless a matched linear effect is source-reconstructable

candidate_sources.citation: Bee phenology is predicted by climatic variation and functional traits
candidate_sources.system: 67 bee species at 18 Rocky Mountain sites, 2009-2017
candidate_sources.current_state: public Dryad source identified; plant comparison must be verified as source-backed and commensurate
candidate_sources.caveat: do not infer plant partner slopes from a different study unless exposure and scale are explicitly harmonized

candidate_sources.citation: Hall et al. 2026, Plant-pollinator interaction potential varies with temperature and precipitation in a dryland ecosystem elevational gradient
candidate_sources.system: dryland elevational gradient; plant flowering and pollinator visitation phenology
candidate_sources.current_state: public Dryad CSVs identified; direct synchrony-vs-temperature candidate

candidate_sources.citation: Kharouba et al. 2018, Global shifts in the phenological synchrony of species interactions over recent decades
candidate_sources.current_state: global synthesis benchmark; article/SI identified, machine-readable source table not yet pinned
candidate_sources.caveat: do not treat published aggregate 6.1 d/decade magnitude as independent row-level data

promotion_gate: At least three independent local plant-pollinator systems yield the same Tier A or Tier B estimand with recoverable uncertainty.
Each effect-size row has a study/system identifier and dependency structure; repeated species/pairs are not treated as independent.
Source-level published results are reproduced within declared tolerance before pooled analysis.
No single study contributes more than 50% of effective inverse-variance weight without a predeclared cap/robust sensitivity.
Leave-one-study-out sign and magnitude are reported.
Tier A/B are never pooled with Tier C.
Only after the local multi-study meta-analysis passes may Paper 2 decide whether to add an E7 result.

cross_system_boundary.licensed_if_promoted: multi-study local plant-pollinator estimate plus the independently reconstructed Usui migration-distance meta-regression can be compared as triangulation of the information-access hypothesis
not_licensed: causal claim that taxonomic identity explains local-versus-migrant differences
single pooled bird-versus-pollinator coefficient unless a common estimand and non-confounded design are demonstrated
